target.title: fix(agents): preserve target agent tool allowlist for subagents
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Spawned subagent sessions can lose tools that are allowed only on the target agent profile.

In the GBrain worker-read path, `main` can spawn `dennis-ritchie`, but `main` does not expose `gbrain_readonly`. Dennis has `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`, yet the child session inherits the parent tool allowlist before the target-agent allowlist is persisted. The result is that a fresh Dennis worker does not receive the configured read-only tool even though the target agent configuration allows it.

## Fix

When creating the initial child session patch for `spawnSubagentDirect`, merge inherited tool allow entries from:

- the caller-provided inherited allowlist
- global subagent tool allowlist config: `tools.subagents.tools.alsoAllow`
- target agent config: `targetAgentConfig.tools.alsoAllow`

This keeps the allowlist scoped to the configured target agent instead of broadening the parent or global runtime tool policy.

## Evidence

Current rebased head:

```text
fcaaf7e31139a5ca4be4de43d1b6ca1afffab50f
```

Focused verification after rebasing onto current upstream `main`:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs \
  src/agents/subagent-spawn.depth-limits.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.test.ts

Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       86 passed (86)
```

Additional checks:

```text
node --check src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts
git diff --check
```

The new regression coverage exercises `main -> dennis-ritchie` where the parent inherited tool allowlist lacks `gbrain_readonly`, but Dennis' target agent config includes `tools.alsoAllow: ["gbrain_readonly"]`; the persisted child session now retains `gbrain_readonly` in `inheritedToolAllow`.

## Real Runtime Reproduction

On the affected deployment after an approved gateway restart, a fresh real Dennis subagent still failed to receive the tool:

```text
Fresh Dennis subagent smoke:
- tool_search for gbrain_readonly returned 0 tools
- ALL_TOOLS had no gbrain/brain/readonly match
- stats/search/query/get_page checks could not run because the tool was absent
```

The gateway policy log for that same fresh Dennis spawn shows the exact failure mode:

```text
agents/tool-policy removed 17 tool(s) via tools.profile (coding): ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via agents.dennis-ritchie.tools.deny: web_fetch
agents/tool-policy removed 7 tool(s) via subagent tools.deny: ...
agents/tool-policy removed 1 tool(s) via inherited tools: gbrain_readonly
```

The deployment config already grants Dennis and Albert `tools.alsoAllow` for `gbrain_readonly`, so this is not a missing config grant or plugin-load issue. The runtime is stripping the target-agent allowed tool from the child session through the inherited allowlist.

## Proof Boundary

Post-fix production proof requires this source fix to be merged/deployed and the protected gateway/runtime refresh to run. Until then, the only honest live proof available is the failure trace above plus the regression proving the fixed child-session envelope retains the target agent's configured allowlist.

## Scope

This PR is source-only. It does not deploy, change config, restart the gateway, or grant write/admin GBrain access.
